### CVE-2011-1020
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2011-02-28 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 41770: Linux Kernel 2.6.32 (Ubuntu 10.04) - '/proc' Handling SUID Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2011-01-17, verified=0)

The proc filesystem implementation in the Linux kernel 2.6.37 and earlier does not restrict access to the /proc directory tree of a process after this process performs an exec of a setuid program, which allows local users to obtain sensitive information or cause a denial of service via open, lseek, read, and write system calls.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2011-1021
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-06-21 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 15774: Linux Kernel < 2.6.37-rc2 - 'ACPI custom_method' Local Privilege Escalation (local/linux, 2010-12-18, verified=1)

drivers/acpi/debugfs.c in the Linux kernel before 3.0 allows local users to modify arbitrary kernel memory locations by leveraging root privileges to write to the /sys/kernel/debug/acpi/custom_method file. NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2010-4347.

### CVE-2011-1082
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2011-04-03 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 35404: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - fs/eventpoll.c epoll Data Structure File Descriptor Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-03-02, verified=1)

fs/eventpoll.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.38 places epoll file descriptors within other epoll data structures without properly checking for (1) closed loops or (2) deep chains, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (deadlock or stack memory consumption) via a crafted application that makes epoll_create and epoll_ctl system calls.

Affected:
- n/a / n/a: affected n/a

### CVE-2011-1083
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2011-04-03 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 35403: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - epoll Nested Structures Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-03-02, verified=1)

The epoll implementation in the Linux kernel 2.6.37.2 and earlier does not properly traverse a tree of epoll file descriptors, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (CPU consumption) via a crafted application that makes epoll_create and epoll_ctl system calls.

### CVE-2011-1479
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-06-21 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 35600: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - 'inotify_init1()' Double-Free Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-04-11, verified=1)

Double free vulnerability in the inotify subsystem in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39 allows local users to cause a denial of service (system crash) via vectors involving failed attempts to create files.  NOTE: this vulnerability exists because of an incorrect fix for CVE-2010-4250.

### CVE-2011-2183
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-06-13 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 35820: Linux Kernel 2.6.x - KSM Local Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-06-02, verified=1)

Race condition in the scan_get_next_rmap_item function in mm/ksm.c in the Linux kernel before 2.6.39.3, when Kernel SamePage Merging (KSM) is enabled, allows local users to cause a denial of service (NULL pointer dereference) or possibly have unspecified other impact via a crafted application.

### CVE-2011-2189
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2011-10-10 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 36425: Linux Kernel 2.6.35 - Network Namespace Remote Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-12-06, verified=1)

net/core/net_namespace.c in the Linux kernel 2.6.32 and earlier does not properly handle a high rate of creation and cleanup of network namespaces, which makes it easier for remote attackers to cause a denial of service (memory consumption) via requests to a daemon that requires a separate namespace per connection, as demonstrated by vsftpd.

### CVE-2011-2918
- Assigner: redhat | Published: 2012-05-24 | Updated: 2024-08-06 | Max CVSS: None
- CWE: n/a
- Exploit-DB 17769: Linux Kernel 3.0.0 - 'perf_count_sw_cpu_clock' event Denial of Service (dos/linux, 2011-09-01, verified=0)

The Performance Events subsystem in the Linux kernel before 3.1 does not properly handle event overflows associated with PERF_COUNT_SW_CPU_CLOCK events, which allows local users to cause a denial of service (system hang) via a crafted application.
